title: Career Roadmap · Cosmetologist
summary: A Cosmetologist specializes in beauty and personal-care services such as skin and hair treatments, makeup, nails and cosmetic product knowledge. Clinical and medical-aesthetic procedures require separate qualifications and authorization where applicable.

about.label: Common pathway
about.text: Class 10 / 12 → Recognized cosmetology or beauty-therapy training → Supervised practical experience → Cosmetologist / Beauty Specialist → Advanced specialization.

blocks.label: Stream
blocks.text: Any stream may be accepted for vocational courses; science may be useful for advanced study of skin, hair and cosmetic ingredients.

blocks.label: Useful subjects
blocks.text: Biology, Chemistry, communication and business studies.

blocks.label: Explore
blocks.text: Skin and hair science, makeup, nail care, hygiene and cosmetic ingredients.

blocks.label: Early skills
blocks.text: Precision, client consultation, sanitation, observation and product knowledge.

blocks.label: Entry route
blocks.text: Certificate, diploma or degree programme, depending on the intended scope of work.

items.text: Diploma in Cosmetology → Broad beauty-service and practical cosmetology skills; scope varies by provider.
Diploma in Beauty Therapy → Skincare, facial treatments and salon services.
Certificate in Hair, Makeup or Nail Technology → Specialist service pathway.
B.Sc. / degree in Cosmetic Science or related subjects → Product formulation, testing or cosmetic-industry roles, where offered.
Chemistry / Pharmacy / relevant science degree → Possible route toward cosmetic product development, subject to programme-specific eligibility.

blocks.label: Important
blocks.text: “Cosmetologist” can mean different things across employers and countries. A beauty diploma does not qualify someone to diagnose skin disease, prescribe medication or perform medical procedures.

blocks.label: Stage 1 — Foundation
blocks.text: Skin and hair science, anatomy basics, hygiene and client consultation.

blocks.label: Stage 2 — Technical skills
blocks.text: Facial treatments, makeup, hair styling, nail care and product selection.

blocks.label: Stage 3 — Supervised practice
blocks.text: Client services, sanitation, contraindication awareness and portfolio development.

blocks.label: Stage 4 — Career readiness
blocks.text: Service pricing, product knowledge, customer retention and salon operations.

blocks.label: Project ideas
blocks.text: Skin-consultation form; cosmetic ingredient comparison; bridal / editorial makeup portfolio; salon hygiene and client-safety checklist.

blocks.label: Skill-training route
blocks.text: B&WSSC-aligned training providers and practical-learning centres.

blocks.label: Private sector
blocks.text: Salons, spas, cosmetics brands, beauty studios and professional makeup teams.

blocks.label: Ideal experience areas
blocks.text: Skincare, hair styling, makeup, nail services and cosmetic-product consultation.
Choose supervised placements with clear hygiene protocols. Internships and jobs are not guaranteed.
